papers.title: AlN/AlGaN heterostructure field-effect transistor power devices advantageous for high-temperature application
papers.summary: We report a high-quality AlN/Al0.73Ga0.27N heterostructure field-effect transistor (HFET) advantageous for high-temperature application. The epitaxial heterostructures exhibit a full width at half maximum of 79 arc sec in the (0002) XRD rocking curve, a surface roughness of 0.35 nm, a room-temperature two-dimensional electron gas density of 1.4 × 1013 cm−2 and mobility of 147 cm2/V/s. Two-terminal mesa breakdown measurements revealed an intrinsic critical electric field of 5.6 MV/cm for a 3 μm gap. AlN/Al0.73Ga0.27N HFET devices with gate–drain spacings of 5, 10, 25, and 50 μm were fabricated, and the breakdown voltages are 990, 1420, 2045, and 4203 V, respectively. Remarkably, the saturated drain current exhibits a positive temperature coefficient, in contrast to the negative coefficient in conventional gallium nitride high-electron-mobility transistors, and the threshold voltage decreases from −9.3 to −7.9 V in the temperature range from 25 to 175 °C. This anomalous behavior is attributed to dominant carrier de-trapping from deep-level traps, confirmed by pulsed I–V measurements, temperature-dependent C–V, and Hall measurements. These observations provide strong evidence for the multi-kilovolt-class and high-temperature power switching applications of the AlN/Al0.73Ga0.27N HFET devices.

papers.title: Depletion-mode N-polar AlN-based high electron mobility transistors on sapphire with improved on/off ratios
papers.summary: We report N-polar AlN-based high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) with a GaN channel thickness of 5.2 nm on N-polar AlN on sapphire. The threshold voltage is around −3.0 to −2.4 V, with saturation currents over 240 mA/mm and on/off ratios as high as 104, much higher than those of previously reported N-polar AlN-based HEMTs. The improved on/off ratio achieved in this work is attributed to the use of an abrupt AlN/GaN heterostructure with a dedicated AlN transition layer, together with improved gate leakage. Both the high-frequency performance and the on-resistance of ≈20 Ω mm are limited by the 2000 Ω/□ sheet resistance of the channel layer.

papers.title: Experimental study of β -Ga2O3 MOSFET with p -NiO source field plate for high-performance
papers.summary: In this work, we demonstrate a lateral Ga2O3 metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistor (MOSFET) with the p-NiO source field plate (PSFP). The PSFP consists of a p-NiO layer above the n-drift, which is shorted to the source electrode and isolated from Ga2O3 by an Al2O3 layer. In the OFF-state, the p-NiO not only modulates the electric field distribution to enhance breakdown voltage (BV) but also assists depleting the n-drift and allows an elevated doping concentration to reduce specific on-resistance (Ron,sp). In the ON-state, the Al2O3 dielectric layer suppresses the NiO-induced n-drift depletion, inhibiting Ron,sp degradation. Through the use of multiple-energy silicon ion implantations into the Ohmic contact regions and subsequent high-temperature annealing, an ultralow Ohmic contact resistance of 0.35 Ω mm is achieved. Compared with conventional MOSFET (Con. MOSFET) and MOSFET with the p-NiO floating field plate (PFFP MOSFET), the fabricated PSFP MOSFET achieves a BV of 2580 V at Nd = 3.5 × 1017 cm−3 and LGD = 25 μm, which is increased by 104% and 94%, respectively; the PSFP MOSFET obtains a power figure of merit of 46.87 MW/cm2, which is increased by 294% and 252%. It is expected that PSFP is a promising technological strategy to fulfill the potential of Ga2O3 for the high-efficiency power conversion.

papers.title: Artificial gauge field modulated on-chip gigahertz acoustic coupling
papers.summary: Phononic integrated circuits (PhICs) represent a promising paradigm for on-chip acoustic information processing. However, conventional straight-waveguide architectures suffer from intrinsically dispersive inter-waveguide coupling, limiting bandwidth and fabrication tolerance. Meanwhile, evanescent crosstalk between adjacent waveguides fundamentally constrains integration density. Here, we introduce an artificial gauge field (AGF) to suppress inter-waveguide coupling dispersion on a CMOS-compatible GaN-on-4H-SiC platform, as validated by the theoretical and experimental demonstration of a broadband 1:1 power divider (PD). Beyond outperforming conventional straight-waveguide directional couplers in broadband performance, the AGF-modulated PD exhibits enhanced robustness against both global offsets and local waveguide-gap perturbations. We further demonstrate the first realization of acoustic coherent destruction of tunneling, enabling crosstalk-free parallel waveguide arrays for densely integrated phononic architectures. Our work thus marks a significant advance toward scalable, high-density, and fabrication-tolerant PhICs.

papers.title: High ambipolar mobility fluorinated MXene for ultrasensitive biosensing transistors
papers.summary: Transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) are emerging as transformative materials for bioelectronics. However, the advancement of MXene-based field-effect transistor (FET) biosensors is hindered by the lack of high-quality aqueous-stable materials and the low signal transduction efficiency intrinsic to their metallic nature. To address these issues, we report an ultrasensitive biosensing platform enabled by an in-situ fluorination strategy of MXene. By substituting unstable oxygen-containing terminations with chemically stable fluorine terminations in a mild reaction, we synthesized high-quality fluorinated MXene with the record-breaking ambipolar field-effect mobility (μ p = 10.42 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , μ n = 30.23 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ). The highly electronegative fluorinated interface suppresses interfacial electrical double-layer capacitance, boosting signal transduction efficiency. Consequently, the platform achieves the lowest limit of detection (LOD) of 0.26 fg ml −1 for Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen MPT64 among MXene FETs up to date, accompanied by a high current response of 35.02% at LOD. Clinical validation across 126 serum samples demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 97.6% with a detection time of 38 s, exhibiting the high-performance and reliable biosensing in complex physiological environments.

papers.title: Self-powered, filter-free, and fast solar-blind photodetectors enabled by luminescent converters with giant Stokes shift
papers.summary: Solar-blind photodetectors (SBPDs) are commonly plagued by trade-offs among superior spectral selectivity, high responsivity, and rapid photoresponse speed. Herein, we report a self-powered SBPD integrated with an Er3+-doped metal halide luminescent converter, nominal composition Cs2Ag0.3Na0.7In0.6Er0.4Cl6, which features an enormous Stokes shift. This luminescent medium converts deep-ultraviolet (DUV) photons into visible emission, which is subsequently captured by a commercial silicon photodiode (Si PD). The converter realizes two integrated functions simultaneously: highly efficient DUV-to-visible photon conversion and intrinsic visible-light rejection, thereby removing the requirement for additional external optical filters. Operated under zero bias, the fabricated device delivers a remarkable responsivity of 226.7 mA/W upon 280 nm irradiation at an optical power of 10 μW, an eightfold enhancement relative to the pristine Si PD. Meanwhile, the photodetector exhibits a prominent photo-to-dark current ratio of approximately 4500. More importantly, the system exhibits an ultrafast photoresponse, with rise and fall times measured at 143 and 77 μs, respectively, which is about three orders of magnitude faster than typical Ga2O3-based SBPDs limited by persistent photoconductivity. The proposed design circumvents the intrinsic material drawbacks of conventional wide-bandgap semiconductors, establishing a strategy for low-cost, high-speed solar-blind photodetection.

papers.title: Modulating and stabilizing MoS2 electronics via a sulfur capping layer
papers.summary: Two-dimensional semiconductors, featuring atomic-scale thickness, excellent electrostatic gate control, and outstanding electrical properties, hold great promise for next-generation electronics. Recently, monolayer MoS2, a typical two-dimensional semiconductor, has been extensively explored for field-effect transistors (FETs). However, its atomically thin channel is highly sensitive to environmental exposure and interfacial perturbations, leading to significant performance degradation. Here, we report a low-temperature (200 °C), intrinsic sulfur passivation strategy to form a nondestructive capping layer on monolayer MoS2 FETs. This capping layer effectively isolates the channel from ambient species while passivating sulfur vacancy defects. As a result, the electrical performance is markedly improved, leading to a positive threshold voltage shift of 1.5 V and a substantial reduction in hysteresis from 2 V to 160 mV. Notably, the devices exhibit excellent environmental stability, maintaining their performance after 180 days under ambient conditions. Based on this approach, rail-to-rail inverters are realized using a pristine MoS2 load transistor and an S-capped MoS2 driver transistor, achieving a high voltage gain of 175.11 with symmetric noise margins (noise margin high ≈ 1.82 V and noise margin low ≈ 1.82 V). Importantly, large-scale inverter arrays demonstrate excellent device uniformity and reproducibility in performance. Furthermore, the scalability of this strategy is demonstrated via various fundamental logic circuits, including NOR and NAND gates, as well as a five-stage ring oscillator. These results highlight the effectiveness of sulfur passivation in enabling high-performance, stable, and scalable MoS2-based electronic and integrated circuit applications.

papers.title: Room-temperature multiferroicity in van der Waals Fe-doped SnSe semiconductors
papers.summary: Two-dimensional materials hosting multiple ferroic orders are highly desirable for next-generation electronic and spintronic technologies. However, achieving stable and tunable ferroic functionalities at room temperature remains a key challenge. Here, we report the growth of van der Waals (vdW) Fe-doped SnSe semiconductor that can be exfoliated down to thin layered flakes. These crystals exhibit tunable ferromagnetism well above room temperature, with the Curie temperature increasing from 342 to over 400 K through controlled Fe incorporation. In parallel, anomalous Hall measurements reveal interfacial spin polarization at the SnSe/Pt interface driven by magnetic proximity effects, enabling spin-dependent magnetotransport. Furthermore, robust ferroelectric behavior at room temperature is confirmed by piezoresponse force microscopy. Although the ferromagnetic and ferroelectric orders coexist within the same material system, they originate from distinct mechanisms without direct magnetoelectric coupling. The semiconducting nature of Fe-doped SnSe is supported by both theoretical and experimental analyses, which further enhances its multifunctionality. These results establish Fe-doped SnSe as a versatile vdW platform for integrating magnetic, electric, and electronic functionalities in future energy-efficient devices.
